pairs.subject: generated-music-acceptance
pairs.evidence: lib/sound/huntRender.ts:353 A hunt render files its take knowing only the provider and a coarse 'music'/'sfx' model, with no account, plan tier, terms date or cleared destination, so a take that is later kept or finalized has no rights record. The measure side of this context is strong: loudness and peak, structure against the brief, and defect counts are all present.

techniques.evidence: lib/sound/measureRun.ts:88 Every ingested blob gets integrated LUFS, true peak, LRA, clipping and tail silence, measured by the sidecar on the original file. The header at :22 explains why it is not taken from the 11 kHz decode. A sidecar failure leaves NULL, never a pass.

lib/sound/measureRun.ts:199 The triage pass checks each take against what its brief committed to: asked length, tempo, loop, and plan sections laid on the take's clock. A check whose number was never committed is skipped, per the 'verify what was committed' rule.

lib/sound/insights.ts:90 Rejects carry classed reasons (types.ts DEFECTS mirrors the taxonomy), counted per provider × term/technique cell with a top defect. That is the recurrence record. Repair/re-render/condemn routing is not encoded.

lib/sound/rubric.ts:47 A judged take is scored on the kind's fixed dimensions (types.ts RUBRIC music: melody, instrument_choice, instrument_quality). These are taste axes, not a checklist built from the brief's own commitments (named exclusions, vocal/instrumental, ending shape).
lib/sound/huntRender.ts:330 A take record holds provider, prompt and terms but no account, plan tier, terms date, model version or cleared destination. The SoundTake type has no such fields at all.

pairs.subject: generated-music-acceptance
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/arrangeActs.ts:3 Finalizing a take gives it the library label agents select by, and it needs only a label. Nothing checks its measured loudness or true peak, and nothing records its rights, so a finalized asset can be unmeasured and uncleared.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/arrangeActs.ts:3 Finalize is a move plus a label (lib/sound/arrange.ts moveTake has no measurement check). The card read at arrangeRead.ts:70 carries length and peaks but not the LUFS or true peak the measure row holds.

app/(studio)/audio/return/route.ts:3 A Suno return is a new audio file filed as the card's next version. fileReturn sets verdict 'kept' from the head (lib/sound/arrange.ts:168), and it can land straight in finalized with no listen of its own.

app/(studio)/audio/return/route.ts:68 A hand-made Suno return brings only bytes, mime and file name: no account, plan tier or terms date. Suno's commercial grant is exactly the plan-scoped, non-retroactive case the technique names.

pairs.subject: generated-music-acceptance
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/leafReturn.ts:62 A Suno leaf rendered by hand in the operator's own Suno session is filed with provider 'suno' and no account, plan tier or terms date, and crowning it makes it a kept take on the Arrange board. The asset reaches the commercial path with no rights record.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/leafReturn.ts:62 The return writes provider and 'manual' op only. Account and plan tier, the load-bearing facts, are never captured.

app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/read.ts:81 The crown is a side-by-side comparative listen, which the technique says needs matched levels. auditionOf passes only peaks (normalised per take) and length, and HuntAudition applies no gain matching, so louder reads as better.
app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/Hunt.tsx:4 A hunt is exploration across axes, which the technique exempts ('slating directions is selection, not acceptance'). The asked chips sit beside each audition take.
